title: Shafarevich-Tate groups of holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations II

candidates.error_location: Theorem A, part (2) (stated in the introduction; proved as Theorem 3.0.7)
candidates.exact_quote:
Theorem A (3.0.6, Theorem 3.0.7). Let \( \pi: X \to B \) be a Lagrangian fibration on an irreducible hyper-kähler manifold \( X \). Pick a class \( \varphi \in \Sha' \), i.e., a class \( \varphi \) such that \( r\varphi \) lies in \( \Sha^0 \) for some positive integer \( r \). Then the following holds.

1. The twist \( X^\varphi \) is Kähler.
2. A twist \( X^\varphi \) with respect to \( \varphi \in \Sha' \) is projective if and only if \( \varphi \) is torsion.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: X is an irreducible hyperkähler manifold (compact, simply connected, Kähler, with H^0(Omega^2_X)=C sigma) with a Lagrangian fibration pi: X -> B; Sha = H^1(B, Aut^0_{X/B}) is the Shafarevich–Tate group, Sha^0 its connected component of unity, and Sha' = {phi in Sha : r*phi in Sha^0 for some r > 0}. For phi in Sha, X^phi denotes the Shafarevich–Tate twist. The paper's Theorem A(2) asserts: for any irreducible hyperkähler X (not assumed projective) and any phi in Sha', X^phi is projective if and only if phi is a torsion element of Sha. Elsewhere the same paper asserts (proof of Corollary 2.1.14, proof of Lemma 5.1.1, proof of Corollary 3.0.8) that for every such X there exists psi in Sha^0 with X^psi projective. Note also that Sha(X) = Sha(X^psi) canonically and (X^psi)^{-psi} = X. The corresponding proved statement, Theorem 3.0.7, is stated only for X projective: 'Let pi: X -> B be a Lagrangian fibration on a projective hyperkähler manifold, and phi in Sha'.'
candidates.suspected_defect: Theorem A(2) drops the projectivity hypothesis that Theorem 3.0.7 carries, and as stated it is self-contradictory: take X non-projective hyperkähler with a Lagrangian fibration and psi in Sha^0 with X^psi projective (the paper asserts such psi exists). Theorem A(2) applied to X forces psi to be torsion; then applying Theorem A(2) with base point X^psi (projective hyperkähler, same group Sha, same twists) to the torsion element -psi forces X = (X^psi)^{-psi} to be projective — contradicting that X was non-projective. Hence the hypothesis 'X projective' is necessary in Theorem A(2).

candidates.exact_quote: (3) ⇒ (1). We can find a torsion element ψ ∈ Ш such that φ − ψ is arbitrarily close to 0. In particular, we may assume that X^{φ−ψ} is Kähler. A cohomology class α has non-zero intersection with η if and only if the restriction of α to a smooth fiber is non-trivial (Theorem 2.1.6). By Theorem 3.0.1 the manifold X^{φ−ψ} carries a rational (1,1)-class α' such that q(α', η) ≠ 0 as well. By [AR21, Lemma 5.15], a hyperkähler manifold with a Lagrangian fibration admitting a (1,1)-class not orthogonal to η is projective. Hence X^{φ−ψ} is projective. By the implication (1) ⇒ (2), the manifold X^φ is projective as well.
candidates.claim_content: In Theorem 3.0.7 (Lagrangian fibration pi: X -> B on a projective hyperkähler manifold, phi in Sha' = classes whose image in (Sha/Sha^0) tensor Q vanishes) several conditions are claimed equivalent; from the proof they are (1) 'phi is torsion', (2) 'X^phi is projective', (3) 'X^phi carries a rational (1,1)-class alpha with q(alpha, eta) != 0', where eta is the pullback to X of an ample generator of Pic(B) and q is the Beauville–Bogomolov–Fujiki form. The proof establishes (1) => (2) ('By Theorem 3.0.1 there is a relatively ample class on X^phi. Hence X^phi is projective.') and (2) => (3) ('An ample class on X^phi will do the job'), and the displayed argument is labelled (3) => (1) but its final sentence concludes 'the manifold X^phi is projective as well', i.e. condition (2).
candidates.suspected_defect: The argument labelled (3) => (1) concludes (2), not (1). Hence the implication 'X^phi projective (or NS(X^phi) not contained in eta^perp) implies phi is torsion' is never proved, and the claimed cycle of equivalences is not closed. This direction is exactly what is used later: Corollary 4.4.3 says 'By Theorem 3.0.7 for a very general t in U, NS(X_t) ⊂ η^⊥', which requires that non-torsion twists have NS inside eta^perp, i.e. precisely the unproved implication. It also underlies Theorem A(2)'s 'only if' direction.

candidates.error_location: Proof of Theorem 2.2.7 (step showing p(W_Q) = p(H^2(X,Q)))
candidates.exact_quote:
The image of \( T_{\mathbb{Q}}(X) \) under the Hodge projection coincides with the image of \( H^2(X, \mathbb{Q}) \). Indeed, the kernel of \( p: H^2(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^{0,2}(X) \) is \( NS_{\mathbb{Q}}(X) \). Therefore,
$$
p(H^2(X, \mathbb{Q})) = p(T_{\mathbb{Q}}(X)) \subset p(W_{\mathbb{Q}}),
$$
candidates.claim_content: Setting: X is an irreducible hyperkähler manifold with a Lagrangian fibration pi: X -> B, q is the Beauville–Bogomolov–Fujiki form on H^2(X,Q) (non-degenerate), p: H^2(X,Q) -> H^{0,2}(X) is the Hodge projection (whose kernel is NS_Q(X)), W_Z is the subgroup of H^2(X,Z) of classes restricting trivially to all fibers (so W_Q = eta^perp, where eta is the pullback of an ample class on B, q(eta)=0), T_Q(X) := NS_Q(X)^perp. The proof asserts p(T_Q(X)) = p(H^2(X,Q)), justified only by 'ker p = NS_Q(X)'. Theorem 2.2.7 concludes that Sha^0 is isogenous to H^{0,2}(X)/p(H^2(X,Z)).
candidates.suspected_defect: p(T_Q) = p(H^2(X,Q)) is equivalent to H^2(X,Q) = NS_Q + T_Q, which holds only if q restricted to NS_Q is non-degenerate. When X is a non-projective hyperkähler manifold with a Lagrangian fibration one has NS(X) ⊂ eta^perp and eta in NS with q(eta)=0, so NS_Q is q-degenerate; then NS_Q ⊂ W_Q = eta^perp and dim p(W_Q) = (b_2 - 1) - dim NS_Q < b_2 - dim NS_Q = dim p(H^2(X,Q)). So p(W_Q) is strictly smaller than p(H^2(X,Q)) and Theorem 2.2.7 (Sha^0 isogenous to H^{0,2}/p(H^2(X,Z))) fails in the non-projective case; the proof step is invalid precisely there.

candidates.exact_quote: Then either \( b_{2}(X^{\varphi}) = b_{2}(X) \) or \( b_{2}(X^{\varphi}) = b_{2}(X) - 1 \). The first case occurs if and only if there is a class \( h \in H^{2}(X) \) whose restriction to a smooth fiber is non-trivial.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: pi: X -> B is a Lagrangian fibration on an irreducible hyperkähler manifold X, X^phi a Shafarevich–Tate twist, F a smooth fiber. Proposition 5.3.9 asserts b_2(X^phi) = b_2(X) or b_2(X) - 1, and that the first case occurs if and only if there is a class h in H^2(X) whose restriction to a smooth fiber is non-trivial. Independently, Theorem 2.1.6 (quoted in the paper) says that for a Lagrangian fibration on a hyperkähler manifold the restriction map H^2(X,Q) -> H^2(F,Q) has rank one, so such a class h in H^2(X) always exists (e.g. a Kähler class).
candidates.suspected_defect: The criterion is stated with H^2(X) instead of H^2(X^phi). Since X is hyperkähler, a class in H^2(X) restricting non-trivially to a smooth fiber always exists (Theorem 2.1.6), so as stated the criterion would always be satisfied and the second alternative b_2(X^phi) = b_2(X) - 1 could never occur — contradicting Theorem C(2) and Remark 5.3.13 (b_2(BG^n(S)) = b_2(K^n(A)) - 1). The proof in fact distinguishes cases according to whether H^2(X^phi) contains such a class.

candidates.exact_quote: By [Huy99, Theorem 3.5] any non-trivial family of deformations of an irreducible hyperkähler manifold contains a projective deformation. Therefore there exists a projective Shafarevich–Tate deformation \(\pi^\psi: X^\psi \to B\) of the Lagrangian fibration \(\pi: X \to B\).
candidates.claim_content: Claim used: 'any non-trivial family of deformations of an irreducible hyperkähler manifold contains a projective deformation', from which the paper deduces that for any Lagrangian fibration pi: X -> B on an irreducible hyperkähler manifold there is psi in Sha^0 with X^psi projective. Recall that for an irreducible hyperkähler X, X is projective iff there exists alpha in NS(X) with q(alpha) > 0 (q = BBF form), and that along the Shafarevich–Tate (degenerate twistor) family the period is [sigma + t eta], t in C, with eta the pullback of an ample class on B, q(eta) = 0 and q(eta, sigma) = 0.
candidates.suspected_defect: The quoted general statement is false as a blanket claim about arbitrary non-trivial families: a one-parameter family of hyperkähler manifolds need not contain any projective fiber (projectivity imposes a countable union of conditions whose intersection with a given curve in the period domain can be empty, e.g. for suitable twistor-type families). The specific conclusion for degenerate twistor families is plausible (one can solve q(alpha, sigma) + t q(alpha, eta) = 0 for suitable integral alpha with q(alpha) > 0 and q(alpha, eta) != 0), but the cited justification does not support it. The conclusion is used repeatedly (Corollary 2.1.14, Corollary 3.0.8, Lemma 5.1.1).

candidates.claim_content: Setting: f_m : Y'_m -> Y_m is an isomorphism of compact hyperkähler manifolds of complex dimension 2n, alpha_m is a Kähler form on Y'_m, beta_m a Kähler form on Y_m, Gamma_m ⊂ Y'_m × Y_m is the graph of f_m, P_1, P_2 the projections onto Y'_m and Y_m, and the volume is computed with respect to P_1^*alpha_m + P_2^*beta_m. Markings are g_t : H^2(Y_t) -> Lambda and g'_t : H^2(Y'_t) -> Lambda with f_t^* = (g'_t)^{-1} ∘ g_t : H^2(Y_t) -> H^2(Y'_t).
candidates.suspected_defect: Type mismatches. (i) f_m^* alpha_m is a form on Y'_m (f_m : Y'_m -> Y_m, alpha_m lives on Y'_m), so 'f_m^* alpha_m' cannot be added to beta_m on Y_m and integrated over Y_m; the correct integrand uses (f_m^{-1})^* alpha_m on Y_m (or one integrates over Y'_m). (ii) In the limit, (g'_0)^{-1} ∘ g_0 maps H^2(Y_0) -> H^2(Y'_0), but it is applied to [alpha_0] in H^2(Y'_0) and the result is added to [beta_0] in H^2(Y_0); the map should be g_0^{-1} ∘ g'_0. candidates.exact_quote: Suppose that the set U ⊂ 𝔻 parametrizing Kähler Shafarevich–Tate deformations of X is non-empty and 0 ∈ U. Then X is hyperkähler.
candidates.claim_content: Proposition 4.0.1: pi: X -> B is a Lagrangian fibration on an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold; X -> D is the restriction of the Shafarevich–Tate (degenerate twistor) family to a disk D ⊂ C^1 with X = X_0 the fiber over 0; U ⊂ D is the set of parameters t for which X_t is Kähler. The hypothesis as stated is '0 ∈ U'; the conclusion is 'X is hyperkähler' (i.e. X_0 is Kähler). The same hypothesis '0 ∈ U' is repeated in Lemma 4.3.6 and Proposition 4.8.3, and the proposition is applied (Theorem A(1), Corollary 3.0.8) in the situation where X_0 is only a limit of Kähler twists.
candidates.suspected_defect: If literally 0 ∈ U, then X_0 is Kähler by definition of U and the conclusion is vacuous; the intended (and needed) hypothesis is 0 ∈ closure(U), i.e. X_0 is a limit of Kähler twists — this is how the proposition is used (via Corollary 3.0.8, which only gives an open dense set of Kähler twists) and how the proof proceeds (taking sequences t_m -> 0 with t_m ∈ V). As stated the hypothesis is wrong/trivializing.

candidates.exact_quote: As before, we denote by η the pullback of an ample class on B to X. If NS(X) ⊄ η^⊥, then X is projective (Theorem 3.0.7), and we are done. Hence we may assume that NS(X) ⊂ η^⊥. In this case NE(X/Y) = NE(X) by Lemma 4.4.1.
candidates.claim_content: Setting: X = X_0 is the fiber over 0 of a Shafarevich–Tate family over a disk D, Kähler for t in U with 0 in the closure of U, and assumed of Fujiki class C; it is NOT yet known to be Kähler (that is the conclusion of Proposition 4.8.3). Theorem 3.0.7 is stated for Lagrangian fibrations on a projective hyperkähler manifold and its proof uses [AR21, Lemma 5.15] ('a hyperkähler manifold with a Lagrangian fibration admitting a (1,1)-class not orthogonal to eta is projective'), i.e. it presupposes the Kähler property. Lemma 4.4.1 is stated as: 'Let pi: X -> B be a Lagrangian fibration on a hyperkähler manifold. Assume NS(X) ⊂ eta^perp. Then all curves on X lie in fibers of pi.'
candidates.suspected_defect: Both Theorem 3.0.7 and Lemma 4.4.1 are invoked for X = X_0, which at this point of the argument is only holomorphic symplectic of Fujiki class C and not known to be Kähler/hyperkähler; their stated hypotheses (projective hyperkähler, resp. hyperkähler) are not satisfied. This looks circular (Kählerness of X is the conclusion being proved). Also 'NE(X/Y)' is undefined (presumably NE(X/B)).

candidates.error_location: Proof of Corollary 4.8.2 (openness of the positivity condition)
candidates.exact_quote: There is a neighborhood U of β inside H¹,¹(X) such that every β′ ∈ U satisfies the assumptions of the corollary.
candidates.claim_content: Corollary 4.8.2: X is a compact holomorphic symplectic manifold of Fujiki class C which is a limit of hyperkähler manifolds; beta in H^{1,1}(X) satisfies (1) q(beta) > 0 (q the BBF form) and (2) beta · c > 0 for any class c in NE(X), the Mori cone generated by classes of curves on X. The proof asserts that there is a neighbourhood U of beta in H^{1,1}(X) such that every beta' in U again satisfies (1) and (2).
candidates.suspected_defect: Condition (2) — strict positivity against every class in the (possibly non-closed, not finitely generated, and without compact base) cone NE(X) — is not obviously an open condition in beta: beta·c > 0 for all c in NE(X)\{0} does not in general imply the same for all nearby beta', unless NE(X) admits a compact base / is locally finitely generated. The proof asserts openness without justification; this is a genuine gap in deducing Corollary 4.8.2 from Theorem 4.8.1.

*Proof.* Let \( t \in V \subset \mathbb{D} \) be such that \( NS(X_t) \not\subset \eta^\perp \).
candidates.claim_content: Setting: X -> D is a Shafarevich–Tate family with Lagrangian fibrations pi_t : X_t -> B (same base B for all t), Y -> D is a family of hyperkähler manifolds with X_t bimeromorphic to Y_t for t in U, and V ⊂ U is the open dense subset of t for which Y_t admits a Lagrangian fibration p_t : Y_t -> B'. The proposition claims B is isomorphic to B' for all t in V, but the proof only treats one particular t in V, namely one with NS(X_t) not contained in eta^perp (hence X_t and Y_t projective), where it invokes [Mat14, Corollary 2] on birational Lagrangian fibrations of projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds.

candidates.claim_content: Setting: Y is a non-projective hyperkähler manifold, bimeromorphic to a hyperkähler manifold X carrying a Lagrangian fibration pi: X -> B with NS(X) ⊂ eta^perp; it is shown that Y contains an open subset isomorphic to X^0 = pi^{-1}(B^0) (the preimage of the locus of smooth fibers), in particular Y contains a Lagrangian torus. The paper's Step 2 asserts, citing [GLR13], that the fibration on this open subset extends to an honest Lagrangian fibration p: Y -> B' (a holomorphic morphism) with B' birational to B.
candidates.suspected_defect: The Greb–Lehn–Rollenske result produces an almost holomorphic (meromorphic) Lagrangian fibration having the given torus as a fiber; concluding the existence of a genuine holomorphic Lagrangian fibration p: Y -> B' onto a base birational to B is stronger than the cited statement and requires additional input (regularity of the almost holomorphic fibration). This affects Corollary 4.4.3 and everything in Section 4 that assumes Y_t carries an honest Lagrangian fibration.
